This discussion is for The Invisible Man by HG Wells, Chapters 1-7.

Chapter 7 ends on page 39 in the document found here

Be aware, spoilers may be in this thread, and the spoiler tag is not mandatory.

Man, I'm not impressed with how he's chosen to act with his invisibility so far. The guy is clearly mad and doesn't understand sound decision making.

Also, it's been so long since I've read classic sci-fi and I forgot what it feels like to have to reference unfamiliar words. I would say it feels good, but I don't see myself using 'serviette' any time soon.

I'm curious to find out how he became invisible. In one of his mutterings at the inn they hear him mention "300,000 or 400,000! Cheated!" (chapter 3). I thought that was possibly how many attempts he's made to reverse what happened to him. And with him saying he was cheated I'm thinking maybe there was a scientific partner involved but maybe he's already dead or unwilling to help out of malice.

If he's been invisible for such a long length of time I could sympathize with his frustration but so far he does come across at someone making some pretty irrational decisions. He has plenty of trunks with him, it seems it would make more sense to steal money from the town he just left and stash it with his belongings as opposed to coming to a new small town and needing to steal from its residents within a few weeks.

I'm also really enjoying stretching my vocabulary but I had to smile when you mentioned serviette because while I've never used the word myself, I do see it in quite often in Canada since it's French for "napkin" :)

I'm really enjoying this book so far, much more than I anticipated to be honest! I've never really been part of a book club so I'm not sure exactly what we're supposed to talk about haha but here's a few things of I've noted so far:

  • I've noticed a bit of subtle religious descriptions which I think are probably to showcase the mindset of the "Sussex peasants". One of the first descriptions of the Man in chapter 1 describes his hair "project[ing] in curious tails and horns" which made me think of a devil immediately. In chapter 3 he is describe as the person who "fell out of infinity" which could read like "falling from heaven", maybe he's going to be a "fallen angel" type character? Or (what I suppose is more likely) a scientist with an Icarus complex, falling after flying too high. And in chapter 7 the "Babel of noise" when he finally uncloaks himself, capitalized intentionally like the Tower of Babel.
  • I liked how when Mrs. Hall first saw him partially uncloaked she saw an "enormous mouth wide open - a vast and incredible mouth" which gave me a chuckle considering how big Mrs. Hall's mouth seems to be thus far.
  • I have no idea if it's important but the fact that he arrived in town on February 29, an unusual date, maybe just underscores that he is an unusual character?

And a couple questions I have:

  • In chapter 7 he is described as "looking more like an angry diving-helmet than ever" but I can't really picture how he displays anger without showing his eyes/eyebrows/mouth, etc. How can goggles over a wrapped face portray emotion?
  • I'm still a little confused on who the narrator is. Chapter 4 started in the first person but I don't think we actually know who the narrator is yet, do we?
